triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: All eight rules started at 2026-02-15, leaving a three-month gap after predecessor heading 9903.02.56 was terminated on November 14, 2025, during which no South Korea reciprocal heading was operative in the encoding.
triage.triage_notes: Read the source: resolve_provision.py on us/statute/hts/9903.02.56 returns "[Compiler's note: This provision was terminated on November 14, 2025. See 90 Fed. Reg. 55964]", which is exactly the excerpt the new effective_period atoms quote. Note the grounding is indirect — the start of successors .79/.80 is inferred from the predecessor's termination date plus a no-gap assumption (the added summary says so: 'the successor headings 9903.02.79-9903.02.80 govern from that handoff date with no gap'), not from a statement in 9903.02.79 itself. Confidence 0.85 rather than 0.9 for that reason; the commit message names the defect and the diff shows exactly it. Same pattern as index 6. No formula changes.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes `effective_from` from '2026-02-15' to '2025-11-14' on all eight rules of the kr-79 module (parameter, threshold judgment, two exception judgments, the floor-applies judgment, and the three duty-rate outputs), so encoded meaning — the version window in which the heading is operative — changed, not just provenance. The date is source-grounded: the pinned corpus text of us/statute/hts/9903.02.56 reads verbatim "[Compiler's note: This provision was terminated on November 14, 2025. See 90 Fed. Reg. 55964]", and the repo's own predecessor module reciprocal-south-korea-9903-02-56.yaml already ended at `effective_to: '2025-11-13'` at the parent commit, so the pre-fix 2026-02-15 start left 2025-11-14 through 2026-02-14 with no operative South Korea reciprocal heading. I tried to refute this as mechanical (the added `corpus_citation_paths` and `effective_period` proof atoms are provenance) but the eight date flips are substantive, and as "coverage never claimed" (2026-02-15 appears in 34 ieepa files as a batch default) but a default that contradicts the source-pinned handoff is a wrong window, not missing precision. wrong_period_or_effective_date is the most specific kind; untraceable_branch would be a worse fit since no formula, branch, or scope changed.
triage.verifier_notes: Verified against the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union (corpus commit d9d6fba0b9): us/statute/hts/9903.02.79 contains no date at all, so the effective date for the successor heading is necessarily cross-sourced; the new proof atoms cite 9903.02.56's compiler's note, which resolves byte-for-byte to the excerpt used in the diff. Corroborating evidence the gap was real: `git show 75a3677870:...reciprocal-south-korea-9903-02-56.yaml` has `effective_from: '2025-08-07'` / `effective_to: '2025-11-13'` on every version, grounded on the same compiler's note. Residual caveat for a reviewer: the new 2025-11-14 start is an inference from the predecessor's termination ("successor governs from that handoff date with no gap") rather than an express effective-date statement for 9903.02.79 itself — the commit body admits as much ("kr-79/80 dates are pinned by the 9903.02.56 compiler's-note termination"), and 90 FR 59281 Annex II (cited for the Nov 14 insertions) covers headings 9903.02.82-.91, not .79/.80. That affects how tightly the new date is grounded, not whether the old one was wrong. The kr-79 companion-test additions in the same commit still use period start/end '2026-02-15', which is inside the new window and therefore not contradictory. Diff also touches only dates plus proof/citation metadata; no formula, input, output, or scope changed.
